subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: A joint venture is a short-term business undertaking jointly by two or more persons who share the profits and losses-

options.A: in proportion to the goods supplied by each of them
options.B: in an agreed ratio
options.C: in the ratio of their capital contributions in every case
options.D: equally, whatever their contributions may have been

answer_html:
Answer: (B) in an agreed ratio.

A joint venture is a short-term business undertaking jointly by two or more persons who share the profits and losses in an agreed ratio. It is a temporary form of business organisation, formed where a project involves higher risk, higher investment or multiple skills which an individual may not be able to master alone, and a Memorandum of Undertaking is signed for the purpose.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The parties to a joint venture are called-

options.A: co-principals
options.B: co-consignors
options.C: co-venturers
options.D: co-partners

answer_html:
Answer: (C) co-venturers.

Among the basic features of a joint venture is that the partners are called co-venturers. A joint venture is a business arrangement in which two or more parties agree to pool their resources for the purpose of accomplishing a specific task, which may be a new project or any other business activity.
topic_text: The parties to a joint venture

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Which of the following is a feature of a joint venture?

options.A: The accounts of the co-venturers are settled a year after dissolution
options.B: A joint venture has no name
options.C: A joint venture is carried on under a registered firm name
options.D: A joint venture continues after the particular venture is complete

answer_html:
Answer: (B) A joint venture has no name.

The basic features of a joint venture are that it is done for a specific purpose and hence has a limited duration, that the partners are called co-venturers, that the profit or loss is shared in the agreed ratio, that the co-venturers may or may not contribute initial capital, that the venture is dissolved once the purpose is over, that the accounts of the co-venturers are settled immediately on dissolution, and that a joint venture has no name.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: As regards the contribution of initial capital by the co-venturers-

options.A: each must contribute capital in the profit sharing ratio
options.B: only one of them may contribute capital and the rest none
options.C: they may or may not contribute initial capital
options.D: each of them must contribute an equal amount of capital

answer_html:
Answer: (C) they may or may not contribute initial capital.

Among the features of a joint venture is that the co-venturers may or may not contribute initial capital. Where no separate set of books is maintained, in particular, no joint bank account is opened and the co-venturers do not contribute in cash at all, the goods being supplied by them out of their own stocks and the expenses being met by them.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: As regards the statute applicable, a joint venture and a partnership differ in that-

options.A: the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to both alike, the difference lying only in the duration of the business
options.B: no enactment is applicable to a joint venture, while the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to a partnership
options.C: the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to a joint venture, while no enactment is applicable to a partnership
options.D: the Indian Contract Act, 1872 applies to a joint venture, while the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to a partnership

answer_html:
Answer: (B) no enactment is applicable to a joint venture, while the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 applies to a partnership.

Among the points of distinction between a joint venture and a partnership, no enactment is applicable to a joint venture, whereas the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 is applicable to a partnership. Other distinctions are that a joint venture is carried on without a firm's name, that it is temporary and ends on the completion of a particular venture, and that a minor is generally not admitted to it.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The relation between the parties in a joint venture and in a consignment is respectively that of-

options.A: principal and agent, and of owners
options.B: buyer and seller, and of owners
options.C: owners, and of buyer and seller
options.D: owners, and of principal and agent

answer_html:
Answer: (D) owners, and of principal and agent.

In a joint venture the relation between the parties is that of owners, whereas in a consignment it is that of the principal and the agent. Correspondingly the ownership of the goods is that of the co-venturers in a joint venture, while in a consignment ownership remains with the consignor though possession passes to the consignee.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The methods of recording joint venture transactions are broadly classified into those where-

options.A: a separate set of books is maintained and those where a separate set of books is not maintained
options.B: the venture earns a profit and those where the venture results in a loss to the co-venturers
options.C: the co-venturers contribute capital and those where they contribute goods out of their own stocks
options.D: a joint bank account is opened and those where the co-venturers operate their own bank accounts

answer_html:
Answer: (A) a separate set of books is maintained and those where a separate set of books is not maintained.

There are different methods of recording joint venture transactions, and they can be broadly classified into two, namely when a separate set of books is maintained and when a separate set of books is not maintained. The second of these is itself of two kinds, one in which each co-venturer records all the transactions and one in which each records only his own transactions, the result being ascertained through a Memorandum Joint Venture Account.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where a separate set of books is maintained, the Joint Venture Account is similar to-

options.A: a Balance Sheet of the venture
options.B: a Trial Balance of the venture
options.C: a Cash Book with two columns
options.D: a Profit and Loss Account

answer_html:
Answer: (D) a Profit and Loss Account.

The Joint Venture Account is similar to a Profit and Loss Account and records all the transactions relating to the activities carried out. Its debit side records all expenses, whether paid personally by the co-venturers or out of the joint bank, and its credit side records all sales, whether to outsiders or to the co-venturers, the net result being either a profit or a loss.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: As regards liability, a joint venture and a partnership differ in that-

options.A: in a joint venture liability is unlimited to the extent of the business and the private estate, while in a partnership it is limited to the capital contributed
options.B: in a joint venture liability is limited to the capital contributed alone, while in a partnership it is limited to the particular adventure concerned
options.C: in both the liability is unlimited, the difference lying only in the manner in which the profits are ultimately shared between the parties
options.D: in a joint venture liability is limited to the adventure concerned, while in a partnership it is unlimited to the extent of the business and the private estate

answer_html:
Answer: (D) in a joint venture liability is limited to the adventure concerned, while in a partnership it is unlimited to the extent of the business and the private estate.

In a joint venture the liability is limited to the adventure concerned, for which the parties agree to contribute capital and share profits or losses, whereas in a partnership the liability is unlimited to the extent of the business and the private estate of the partners. A joint venture is also generally local, while a partnership may be located at different places.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The profit earned in a joint venture and the profit earned on a consignment belong respectively to-

options.A: the party managing the venture, and the consignee
options.B: the party contributing the funds, and the consignor
options.C: the co-venturers, and the consignor
options.D: the co-venturers, and the consignee

answer_html:
Answer: (C) the co-venturers, and the consignor.

In a joint venture the profit belongs to the co-venturers, whereas on a consignment the profit belongs to the consignor and not to the consignee. Consistently with this, the co-venturers enjoy full powers to manage the business and contribute funds for it, while the consignee, being an agent, has no power to manage the business and has simply to obey the instructions of his principal.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where a separate set of books is maintained for a joint venture, the accounts opened are-

options.A: the Joint Venture Account, the Trading Account and the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
options.B: the Joint Venture Account, the Joint Bank Account and the Co-venturers' Accounts
options.C: the Joint Venture Account, the Memorandum Joint Venture Account and the Co-venturers' Accounts
options.D: the Joint Venture Account, the Joint Bank Account and the Goods Sent on Joint Venture Account

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the Joint Venture Account, the Joint Bank Account and the Co-venturers' Accounts.

As the duration of the business is short, the books of account are not comprehensive and the basic purpose is to know the profit or loss on the venture, so only three accounts are maintained, namely the Joint Venture Account, the Joint Bank Account and the Co-venturers' Accounts. The balance of a co-venturer's account represents his claim to or from the business, which is ultimately settled through the Joint Bank Account.
topic_text: Accounts under the separate books method

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: In the Joint Bank Account-

options.A: only the sale proceeds and the expenses paid out of the venture funds are recorded
options.B: all cash inflows are recorded on the debit side and all outflows on the credit side
options.C: all cash outflows are recorded on the debit side and all inflows on the credit side
options.D: only the contributions of the co-venturers and the final settlement are recorded

answer_html:
Answer: (B) all cash inflows are recorded on the debit side and all outflows on the credit side.

The Joint Bank Account is maintained to record all cash and bank transactions and may take the form of a cash book with cash and bank columns. It records the initial contributions made by each co-venturer, the proceeds of sales, the expenses and the distribution of the net balances among the co-venturers on dissolution, all cash inflows being recorded on the debit side and the outflows on the credit side.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The debit side of the Joint Venture Account records all expenses-

options.A: paid out of the joint bank alone, those paid personally being ignored
options.B: paid personally by the co-venturers alone, those paid out of the joint bank being ignored
options.C: irrespective of their nature, that is, whether capital or revenue
options.D: of a revenue nature alone, capital expenditure being carried to the Balance Sheet

answer_html:
Answer: (C) irrespective of their nature, that is, whether capital or revenue.

In the Joint Venture Account, the debit side records all expenses, whether paid personally by the co-venturers or out of the joint bank, and irrespective of their nature, that is whether capital or revenue. This follows from the short duration of the venture, in which no distinction between capital and revenue expenditure serves any purpose.
generation_source: Self-authored practice MCQ, based on ICMAI Study Material

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where a separate set of books is maintained and unsold goods are taken over by a co-venturer, the entry passed is-

options.A: Joint Bank A/c Dr., to Joint Venture A/c
options.B: Joint Venture A/c Dr., to Joint Bank A/c
options.C: Co-Venturers A/c Dr., to Joint Venture A/c
options.D: Joint Venture A/c Dr., to Co-Venturers A/c

answer_html:
Answer: (C) Co-Venturers A/c Dr., to Joint Venture A/c.

Unsold goods taken over by a co-venturer are recorded by debiting the Co-Venturers A/c and crediting the Joint Venture A/c, the goods so taken over being in the nature of a sale to him. The reverse entry, debiting the Joint Venture A/c and crediting the Co-Venturers A/c, is used where goods are sent by a co-venturer out of his own stock or where he pays expenses.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Where no separate set of books is maintained for the joint venture-

options.A: a joint bank account is still opened, but the co-venturers do not contribute in cash, the venture being financed entirely out of the sale proceeds realised
options.B: no joint bank account is opened, but the co-venturers must contribute in cash, the amounts being held by one of them on behalf of all
options.C: a joint bank account is opened by each co-venturer separately, and each records only the transactions which he has himself effected
options.D: no joint bank account is opened and the co-venturers do not contribute in cash, each preparing a Joint Venture A/c and the other co-venturer's account in his own books

answer_html:
Answer: (D) no joint bank account is opened and the co-venturers do not contribute in cash, each preparing a Joint Venture A/c and the other co-venturer's account in his own books.

The co-venturers may decide not to keep separate books of account for the venture if it is for a very short period of time. In that case no joint bank account is opened and the co-venturers do not contribute in cash, goods being supplied by them out of their own stocks and the expenses of the venture being met by them. Each co-venturer prepares a Joint Venture A/c and the other co-venturer's account in his own books, so the profit or loss is separately calculated by each.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: The word 'memorandum' is prefixed to the Memorandum Joint Venture Account because-

options.A: the account records only those transactions which are not otherwise recorded
options.B: the account is not a part and parcel of the double entry system
options.C: the account is prepared only from the memoranda kept by the co-venturers
options.D: the account is a mere estimate which is replaced by the final account later

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the account is not a part and parcel of the double entry system.

Under this method each co-venturer records only those joint venture transactions which are effected by him, through a personal account styled Joint Venture with the name of the other co-venturer. Each sends the other a periodic statement of his own transactions, and on receiving it each prepares a Memorandum Joint Venture Account to ascertain the profit or loss. Since this account is not a part and parcel of the double entry system, the word memorandum is prefixed to it.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Aditya and Amit shared profits equally. Aditya contributed ₹2,00,000 and Amit ₹1,50,000 to a joint bank account, Aditya supplied idols worth ₹25,000 and Amit decoration material worth ₹15,000, and the venture paid ₹2,50,000 for idols, ₹12,000 transport, ₹7,500 advertising and ₹2,500 sundry expenses. Sales were ₹4,00,000, and Aditya and Amit took over unsold idols for ₹30,000 and ₹10,000 respectively. The share of profit of each is-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹64,000.

The Joint Venture Account is debited with the materials supplied of ₹25,000 and ₹15,000 and the payments of ₹2,50,000, ₹12,000, ₹7,500 and ₹2,500, making ₹3,12,000 in all. It is credited with sales of ₹4,00,000 and the goods taken over of ₹30,000 and ₹10,000, making ₹4,40,000. The profit is therefore ₹1,28,000, and as profits are shared equally each takes ₹64,000; the ₹1,28,000 in Option (D) is the whole profit and not the share of each.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Ram was entitled to a commission of 5% on sales in a joint venture in which sales amounted to ₹20,800. The commission credited to him is-
answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹1,040.

The commission is 5% of the sales of ₹20,800, that is ₹1,040. It is recorded by debiting the Joint Venture Account and crediting the Commission Account in Ram's own books, and is charged before the profit of the venture is arrived at and divided.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: John sold 500 bales of suiting at ₹600 each and 400 bales of shirting at ₹650 each, and was entitled to commission of 2.5% on total sales together with an allowance of ₹2,000 for looking after the business. The total amount charged to the Joint Venture Account in his favour is-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹16,000.

The total sales are 500 bales at ₹600, that is ₹3,00,000, plus 400 bales at ₹650, that is ₹2,60,000, giving ₹5,60,000. Commission at 2.5% on ₹5,60,000 is ₹14,000, to which is added the allowance of ₹2,000, so ₹16,000 in all is charged to the Joint Venture Account. Option (C) omits the allowance.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
case_facts_html:
Prabir and Mihir, building contractors, undertook jointly to build a skyscraper for a newly started public limited company for a contract price of ₹1,00,00,000, payable ₹80,00,000 in cash and the balance in fully paid equity shares of that company.

A joint bank account was opened, into which Prabir paid ₹25,00,000 and Mihir ₹15,00,000. Profits and losses are shared in the ratio of 2:1 between Prabir and Mihir respectively.

An advance of ₹50,00,000 was received from the company. Wages of ₹10,00,000, materials of ₹60,00,000 and architect's fees of ₹21,00,000 were paid out of the joint bank account. Prabir supplied materials worth ₹10,00,000 and Mihir materials worth ₹15,00,000 out of their own stocks.

The contract was completed and the price duly paid. The venture was closed by Prabir taking over all the shares at ₹18,00,000 and Mihir taking over the balance of the material for ₹3,00,000.
question_html: Refer to the first case scenario. The result of the joint venture is-

options.A: a loss of ₹15,00,000
options.B: a profit of ₹15,00,000
options.C: a loss of ₹13,00,000
options.D: a profit of ₹2,00,000

answer_html:
Answer: (A) a loss of ₹15,00,000.

The Joint Venture Account is debited with wages ₹10,00,000, materials ₹60,00,000, architect's fees ₹21,00,000, materials supplied by Prabir ₹10,00,000 and by Mihir ₹15,00,000 and the loss on shares of ₹2,00,000, making ₹1,18,00,000. It is credited with the advance of ₹50,00,000, the balance of the price ₹30,00,000, the shares received of ₹20,00,000 and the material taken over by Mihir of ₹3,00,000, making ₹1,03,00,000. The venture therefore results in a loss of ₹15,00,000.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
case_facts_html:
Bharat and Sujit joined together as co-venturers for an equal share in the profits from the sale of television cabinets. On 31 March 2023 Bharat purchased 2,000 cabinets at ₹1,250 each for cash and sent 1,500 of them to Sujit for sale, the selling price of each cabinet being ₹1,300.

All the cabinets were sold by 30 April 2023 by the two venturers and the proceeds were collected. Bharat met freight and insurance of ₹12,000 and selling expenses of ₹5,000, while Sujit met clearing charges of ₹1,000 and selling expenses of ₹12,000.

Each venturer records in his own books only those transactions concluded by him, the final profit or loss being ascertained through a Memorandum Joint Venture Account. The final settlement between them took place on 31 May 2023.
question_html: Refer to the second case scenario. The total sale proceeds of the venture are-
answer_html:
Answer: (D) ₹26,00,000.

Bharat sold the 500 cabinets he retained at ₹1,300 each, realising ₹6,50,000, and Sujit sold the 1,500 cabinets sent to him at ₹1,300 each, realising ₹19,50,000. The total sale proceeds are therefore ₹26,00,000, against a purchase cost of 2,000 cabinets at ₹1,250 each, that is ₹25,00,000.

answer_html:
Answer: (A) Sujit pays Bharat ₹19,02,000.

Sujit collected ₹19,50,000 but met expenses of ₹13,000 and is entitled to his share of profit of ₹35,000, so the balance due from him is ₹19,50,000 less ₹48,000, that is ₹19,02,000, which he pays to Bharat. Bharat, who paid for the whole of the stock, is the party to whom the settlement is due.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
case_facts_html:
Bharat and Sujit joined together as co-venturers for an equal share in the profits from the sale of television cabinets. On 31 March 2023 Bharat purchased 2,000 cabinets at ₹1,250 each for cash and sent 1,500 of them to Sujit for sale, the selling price of each cabinet being ₹1,300.

All the cabinets were sold by 30 April 2023 by the two venturers and the proceeds were collected. Bharat met freight and insurance of ₹12,000 and selling expenses of ₹5,000, while Sujit met clearing charges of ₹1,000 and selling expenses of ₹12,000.

Each venturer records in his own books only those transactions concluded by him, the final profit or loss being ascertained through a Memorandum Joint Venture Account. The final settlement between them took place on 31 May 2023.
question_html: Refer to the second case scenario. The total of the Joint Venture with Sujit Account in the books of Bharat is-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹25,52,000.

In Bharat's books the account is debited with the purchases of ₹25,00,000, freight and insurance ₹12,000, selling expenses ₹5,000 and his share of profit ₹35,000, making ₹25,52,000, and is credited with his own sale proceeds of ₹6,50,000 and the settlement of ₹19,02,000 received from Sujit, which also comes to ₹25,52,000. Only the transactions effected by Bharat himself appear in it.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: John and Smith shared profits in the ratio 5:3. John supplied 400 bales of shirting at ₹500 each and paid ₹18,000 for carriage and insurance, Smith supplied 500 bales of suiting at ₹480 each and paid ₹22,000 for advertisement and carriage, total sales were ₹5,60,000, and John took commission of 2.5% on sales and an allowance of ₹2,000. The profit of the venture and John's share of it are respectively-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹64,000 and ₹40,000.

The charges against the venture are the shirting ₹2,00,000, carriage and insurance ₹18,000, the suiting ₹2,40,000, advertisement and carriage ₹22,000, commission ₹14,000 and the allowance ₹2,000, amounting to ₹4,96,000. Against sales of ₹5,60,000 the profit is ₹64,000, of which John's five-eighths share is ₹40,000 and Smith's three-eighths share is ₹24,000.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: M and N guaranteed the subscription at par of 10,00,000 shares of ₹1 each, in consideration of 50,000 fully paid shares and a commission of 5% in cash to be taken in the ratio 3:2. N paid ₹30,000 for shares not subscribed, M met expenses of ₹10,000 and N of ₹5,000, and the holdings were sold, N receiving ₹18,000 and M ₹50,000. If profits are shared three-fourths to M and one-fourth to N, M's share of the profit is-
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹54,750.

The Memorandum Joint Venture Account is credited with the commission of 5% on ₹10,00,000, that is ₹50,000, split three-fifths to M and two-fifths to N, and with the sale proceeds of ₹50,000 and ₹18,000, making ₹1,18,000. It is debited with the cost of the shares ₹30,000 and the expenses of ₹10,000 and ₹5,000, making ₹45,000. The profit is ₹73,000, of which M's three-fourths share is ₹54,750 and N's one-fourth share is ₹18,250.

subject: Fundamentals of Financial and Cost Accounting
question_html: Ram, Mohan and Rahim each contributed ₹5,000 to a joint venture and shared profits equally. Rahim supplied goods worth ₹1,500 from stock and incurred ₹50 of expenses, and his share of the profit of ₹4,460 was taken as ₹1,487. The amount remitted to Rahim in settlement is-
answer_html:
Answer: (A) ₹8,037.

Rahim's account is credited with his contribution of ₹5,000, the goods and expenses of ₹1,550 and his share of profit of ₹1,487, that is ₹8,037, and there is nothing on the debit side, since it was Mohan and not Rahim who took over the unsold goods. The whole of ₹8,037 is therefore remitted to him by bank draft, Mohan receiving ₹5,987 after deducting the goods of ₹500 taken over by him.
